practiceQuestions.q: Under which Article of the Indian Constitution is a National Emergency declared?
practiceQuestions.sol: Article 352 of the Constitution provides for the proclamation of a National Emergency by the President. Article 356 deals with President's Rule in states, and Article 360 deals with Financial Emergency.

practiceQuestions.q: Which of the following terms was substituted for 'internal disturbance' by the 44th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1978?
practiceQuestions.sol: The 44th Amendment Act of 1978 substituted the words 'internal disturbance' with 'armed rebellion' as one of the grounds for proclaiming a National Emergency to prevent its misuse.

practiceQuestions.q: Who has the constitutional power to proclaim a National Emergency?
practiceQuestions.sol: The President proclaims a National Emergency. However, this can only be done on the written recommendation of the Union Cabinet.

practiceQuestions.q: Within what period must a proclamation of National Emergency be approved by both Houses of Parliament?
practiceQuestions.sol: A proclamation of National Emergency must be approved by both Houses of Parliament within one month from the date of its issue (reduced from 2 months by the 44th Amendment Act, 1978).

practiceQuestions.q: By what majority must the resolution approving the proclamation of National Emergency be passed in each House of Parliament?
practiceQuestions.sol: The resolution approving the proclamation of emergency or its continuance must be passed by either House of Parliament by a special majority (a majority of the total membership of that house and a majority of not less than two-thirds of the members present and voting).

practiceQuestions.q: What is the maximum period up to which a National Emergency can be extended, provided parliamentary approval is renewed every six months?
practiceQuestions.sol: Once approved by Parliament, the National Emergency continues for six months and can be extended to an indefinite period with approval of the Parliament every six months.

practiceQuestions.q: Which Fundamental Rights cannot be suspended even during a National Emergency under Articles 359 and 358?
practiceQuestions.sol: By the 44th Amendment Act, 1978, the right to protection in respect of conviction for offences (Article 20) and the right to life and personal liberty (Article 21) cannot be suspended even during a National Emergency.

practiceQuestions.q: How many times has a National Emergency been declared in India so far?
practiceQuestions.sol: A National Emergency has been declared three times in India: in 1962 (Chinese aggression), 1971 (Pakistani aggression), and 1975 (internal disturbance).

practiceQuestions.q: Who can revoke a proclamation of National Emergency at any time?
practiceQuestions.sol: A proclamation of National Emergency may be revoked by the President at any time by a subsequent proclamation. Such a proclamation does not require parliamentary approval.

practiceQuestions.q: Which amendment added the requirement of 'written recommendation' of the Cabinet for declaring a National Emergency?
practiceQuestions.sol: The 44th Amendment Act, 1978 introduced the safeguard that the President can declare a National Emergency only when the decision of the Union Cabinet (Prime Minister and other ministers of cabinet rank) is communicated in writing.

practiceQuestions.q: How does the declaration of a National Emergency affect the legislative powers of the Parliament and State Legislatures?
opts: Parliament acquires the power to make laws for any state on any subject enumerated in the State List.
State legislatures cannot pass any laws concurrently.
Parliament's laws override state laws only with the consent of the Governor.
practiceQuestions.sol: While state legislatures are not suspended, Parliament acquires concurrent power to legislate on subjects enumerated in the State List during a National Emergency. A law made by Parliament ceases to have effect six months after the emergency ceases to operate.

practiceQuestions.q: What is the distinction between the operation of Article 358 and Article 359 regarding Fundamental Rights?
opts: Article 358 automatically suspends Article 19, whereas Article 359 requires a separate Presidential order to suspend the right to move courts for enforcement of other Fundamental Rights.
Article 359 suspends Article 21, whereas Article 358 does not affect any rights.
Article 358 applies only to external aggression, while Article 359 applies only to armed rebellion.
There is no functional distinction; both deal identically with all fundamental rights.
practiceQuestions.sol: Article 358 operates automatically to suspend Article 19 the moment a National Emergency is declared on grounds of war or external aggression (not armed rebellion). Article 359 does not suspend rights automatically; it empowers the President to suspend the right to move any court for enforcing specified Fundamental Rights through an order.

practiceQuestions.q: How does a National Emergency affect the normal financial relations between the Centre and the States?
opts: The President can modify the constitutional distribution of revenues between the Centre and the States.
All tax collections by states are permanently transferred to the Consolidated Fund of India.
The Finance Commission takes over all budgetary allocations.
States are prohibited from collecting any taxes whatsoever.
practiceQuestions.sol: Under Article 354, the President can direct that all or any of the constitutional provisions regarding the distribution of revenues between the Centre and the States shall-remain suspended or be modified during a National Emergency.

practiceQuestions.q: What happens to the tenure of the Lok Sabha when a National Emergency is in operation?
opts: It is automatically extended by 5 years.
It can be extended by Parliament for a period not exceeding one year at a time.
It remains unaffected and elections must be held on time.
It is dissolved by the Supreme Court.
practiceQuestions.sol: During a National Emergency, the Parliament can extend the normal life of the Lok Sabha by one year at a time for any length of time, but not beyond six months after the emergency has ceased to operate.

practiceQuestions.q: Which constitutional amendment introduced the provision enabling 1/10th of the Lok Sabha members to requisition a special sitting to disapprove a National Emergency?
practiceQuestions.sol: The 44th Amendment Act, 1978 added a safeguard: if 1/10th of the Lok Sabha members give a written notice to the Speaker (or President if the House is not in session), a special sitting of the House must be held within 14 days to consider a resolution disapproving the continuation of the emergency.

practiceQuestions.q: What was the judicial status of the proclamation of National Emergency prior to the 44th Amendment Act, 1978?
opts: It was fully subject to judicial review.
It was immune from judicial review under the 38th Amendment Act.
It required prior approval of the Supreme Court.
It could only be reviewed by the High Court of Delhi.
practiceQuestions.sol: The 38th Amendment Act of 1975 made the declaration of National Emergency immune from judicial review. However, the 44th Amendment Act of 1978 removed this provision, making the proclamation subject to judicial review on grounds of mala fide or extraneous considerations.

practiceQuestions.q: How does a National Emergency alter the federal character of the Indian polity?
opts: It converts the federal system into a unitary system without any formal structural division.
It abolishes all state governments permanently.
It strengthens federal autonomy by empowering regional forces.
It has no impact on Centre-State administrative relations.
practiceQuestions.sol: During a National Emergency, the executive and legislative power of the Centre extends to giving directions to states on any matter, effectively turning the normally federal polity into a unitary state.

practiceQuestions.q: What is the consequence if the Lok Sabha is dissolved when a National Emergency has been proclaimed and the emergency resolution is pending approval?
opts: The proclamation survives until 30 days from the date the newly elected Lok Sabha first sits, provided it is approved by the Rajya Sabha in the meantime.
The Rajya Sabha alone can approve it indefinitely.
The Prime Minister must step down immediately.
practiceQuestions.sol: If the Lok Sabha is dissolved without approving the proclamation, or if its approval period expires during dissolution, the proclamation survives until 30 days from the first sitting of the newly elected Lok Sabha, provided Rajya Sabha has approved it.

practiceQuestions.q: Can a National Emergency be proclaimed in respect of a specified part of the territory of India?
opts: No, it must apply to the entire country uniformly.
Yes, the 42nd Amendment Act enabled the proclamation of a National Emergency to be made operationally restricted to a part of the country.
Yes, but only with the consent of the Chief Minister of that state.
No, regional emergencies can only be proclaimed under Article 356.
practiceQuestions.sol: The 42nd Amendment Act of 1976 amended Article 352 to enable the President to proclaim a National Emergency in a specified part of India as well as the whole of India.

practiceQuestions.q: What role does the executive power of the Union play over the States during a National Emergency?
opts: The Union executive can give directions to any state regarding the manner inWhich its executive power is to be exercised.
The Union executive takes over the portfolios of state ministers directly.
State executive powers are completely suspended and replaced by military governors.
The Union executive can only advise states but cannot issue binding directions.
practiceQuestions.sol: During a National Emergency, the executive power of the Centre extends to giving directions to any state regarding the exercise of its executive powers, ensuring that state executive power is exercised in subordination to Union directives.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the grounds for proclaiming a National Emergency:
1. A National Emergency can be declared only on the grounds of war, external aggression, or internal disturbance.
2. The ground of 'armed rebellion' was added to Article 352 by the Constitution (Forty-Fourth Amendment) Act, 1978.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect because 'internal disturbance' was replaced by 'armed rebellion' in 1978. Statement 2 is correct: the 44th Amendment Act, 1978 replaced 'internal disturbance' with 'armed rebellion' as one of the explicit grounds.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding parliamentary approval and duration of a National Emergency:
1. Every resolution approving the proclamation of emergency or its continuance must be passed by a special majority in both Houses of Parliament.
2. The initial proclamation of emergency remains in force for two months unless approved by Parliament.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct; both initial approval and subsequent extensions require a special majority. Statement 2 is incorrect because the initial proclamation must be approved within one month (not two months) by Parliament.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the revocation of a National Emergency:
1. A proclamation of emergency can be revoked by the President at any time by a subsequent proclamation.
2. A proclamation of emergency must be revoked if the Lok Sabha passes a resolution disapproving its continuation by a simple majority.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. Under Article 352, the President can revoke it anytime. Furthermore, as per the 44th Amendment, if 1/10th of Lok Sabha members requisition a sitting and pass a resolution disapproving the emergency by a simple majority, the President is bound to revoke it.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the impact of National Emergency on Fundamental Rights:
1. Article 358 automatically suspends the freedoms guaranteed under Article 19 for all grounds of emergency.
2. Article 359 empowers the President to suspend the right to move any court for the enforcement of Fundamental Rights except Articles 20 and 21.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect because Article 358 operates only when the emergency is declared on the grounds of war or external aggression, NOT on the ground of armed rebellion. Statement 2 is correct.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the 44th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1978 in relation to National Emergency:
1. It deleted the provision that made the proclamation of National Emergency immune from judicial review.
2. It introduced the requirement that the decision to proclaim an emergency must be taken by the Union Cabinet in writing.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. The 44th Amendment Act, 1978 introduced multiple safeguards, including making the proclamation judicially reviewable and mandating written cabinet advice.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding Centre-State legislative relations during a National Emergency:
1. Parliament can make laws on State List subjects even if the emergency is restricted to a specific part of India.
2. Laws made by Parliament on State List subjects during an emergency become permanently operational unless repealed by state legislatures.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct; if emergency is in a part of the country, Parliament can make laws for that or any other part as required. Statement 2 is incorrect because laws made by Parliament on State List subjects cease to have effect on the expiration of six months after the emergency has ceased to operate.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the historic National Emergencies declared in India:
1. The first National Emergency was declared in October 1962 during the Chinese aggression.
2. The third National Emergency in 1975 was declared on the ground of armed rebellion.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct (declared in Oct 1962 due to Chinese aggression and lasted till Jan 1968). Statement 2 is incorrect because the 1975 emergency was declared on the ground of 'internal disturbance', not 'armed rebellion' (which term was introduced later in 1978).

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the extension of the Lok Sabha term during a National Emergency:
1. The normal term of the Lok Sabha can be extended by an act of Parliament for one year at a time during a National Emergency.
2. Such an extension can continue indefinitely even after the emergency has ceased to operate, provided a cabinet resolution supports it.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is incorrect because the extended term cannot continue beyond a period of six months after the emergency has ceased to operate.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the protection under Article 359:
1. An order under Article 359 can suspend the enforcement of all Fundamental Rights without exception.
2. The suspension of enforcement under Article 359 can be extended to the entire country or restricted to any part of it.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect because rights guaranteed under Articles 20 and 21 can never be suspended even under Article 359. Statement 2 is correct; Presidential orders under Article 359 can be applied nationwide or regionally.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the approval requirements for National Emergency:
1. Both the Lok Sabha and the Rajya Sabha must approve the proclamation of emergency within one month by a special majority.
2. If the Rajya Sabha approves the proclamation within one month, but Lok Sabha is dissolved during this period without passing the resolution, the proclamation automatically lapses.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct in stating the one-month period and special majority requirement for both houses. Statement 2 is incorrect: if Lok Sabha is dissolved while the resolution is pending or before approval, the proclamation survives for 30 days from the first sitting of the newly elected Lok Sabha, provided Rajya Sabha has already approved it.
